jobs.title: Head of Platform & Infrastructure Engineering
jobs.description:
Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future.

We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you!

The Role

In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include:

Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.
Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).
Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!
Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.
Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.
You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.
If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!

The Qualifications

We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.
You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.
You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.
You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.
You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe.
You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.

What We’re Building

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better
at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

Why You Shouldn’t Apply

You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.
You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.
You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).
You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.
To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.
You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.

Engineering Culture

Our Engineering Culture Is Motivated By Benji’s (Co-founder And CEO) And My Belief That a Small, Talented Team, Given The Right Environment, Can Build High-quality Software Fast (and Work Regular Hours!). We Do It Through

Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design
Natural collaboration and deliberate communication
Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.
Putting effort into building a diverse team

Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive .

Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).

To Drive It Home, Here's a Recent Calendar Of An Engineer Who Has Been With Us For Over 4 Years. ~34 Hours Of Focus Time, 2.5h Of Interviews, And 3.5 Hours Of Meetings

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

Increase Leverage, not Team Size

We Built Ashby With The Quality, Breadth, And Depth That Many Customers Would Expect From Much Larger Teams Over Larger Time Scales. We’ve Done This Through Investment In

Great developer tooling. For example, our CI/CD takes ~10m, we deploy at least 15x a day, and our debugger works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.
Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).
AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.

And a Demo Of One Of These Building Blocks

jobs.title: AVP HR Service Delivery & Technology
jobs.description:
Job Description

Mackenzie Investments

IGM Financial Inc. is a leading wealth and asset management company in Canada, managing approximately $ 310 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025 . It offers financial planning and investment services to over two million Canadians through IG Wealth Management and Mackenzie Investments.

Mackenzie Investments, founded in 1967, is a key part of IGM's business model, serving as a comprehensive asset-management partner for Canadian financial advisors and their clients.

At Mackenzie Investments You Can Build Your Career with Confidence
.
We are proud to be recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers for the fourth consecutive year and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers. Our vision and strategy aim to innovate the industry and support Canadians in achieving their financial goals.

Join our team to engage in continuous learning and skill development in a supportive environment. Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work environment, where you spend three days a week in the office, connecting, collaborating, and enjoying quality time with your amazing colleagues ! Our Values: Be better ; we strive for improvement in everything we do . Be accountable ; we foster clarity and are empowered to act responsibly . Be a team ; we are united to drive collective impact to achieve our goals .

The Role:
This is an opportunity to shape how HR works and how people experience HR at IGM. As AVP, HR Services Delivery and Technology, you will help turn our future-state service model into a practical, multi-year roadmap and lead the evolution of the technology and services that support it.

You will bring together HR service delivery, HR operations and HR technology so that people can find answers, complete transactions and access support with less friction. You will work closely with the HR Leadership Team, HR Centres of Expertise, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance and business leaders to simplify work, clarify ownership and use technology where it creates real value.

Your work will directly influence employee and leader experience, service quality, operational efficiency and HR’s capacity to focus on higher-value work. It is a role for a leader who is comfortable connecting strategy to execution and building the capabilities, governance and teams needed to make change stick.

Key Responsibilities

Partner with HR Leadership and the Centres of Expertise to implement the future service model, moving appropriate work into scalable self-service, automated and centralized delivery while maintaining clear tiering, ownership and escalation paths.
Translate HR priorities into an integrated roadmap across SAP SuccessFactors, ServiceNow and other HR platforms. Reduce fragmentation, duplicate entry and unnecessary hand-offs so HR feels like one connected experience.
Lead the implementation and ongoing evolution of ServiceNow as HR’s digital front door. Simplify processes, strengthen knowledge management and expand automation and AI-enabled services while preserving appropriate controls and human judgment for complex or sensitive matters.
Provide business leadership and oversight for the HR technology portfolio, holding internal teams and delivery partners accountable for execution, platform health, adoption and value realization.
Set meaningful service standards and measures for case resolution, service levels, experience, quality and risk. Use operational data and feedback to identify root causes, reduce recurring demand and continuously improve services.
Build effective partnerships across HR, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance and the business. Operationalize agreed governance and decision rights, and lead the change required to adopt new ways of working.
Lead a multidisciplinary HR Services & Technology organization and develop the leaders, digital, service and analytical capabilities needed to operate as an integrated, employee-focused function.

Required Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in Human Resources, Business Administration or a related field.
12+ years of progressive leadership experience in HR operations, service delivery, HR technology or a related field within a large, complex organization, including enterprise transformation and team leadership.
Demonstrated experience in service ownership, operating model design, technology roadmap ownership, data-led service leadership, and risk and governance leadership.
Strong change leadership and executive influence, with the ability to work across functions and establish clear accountability and decision rights.
Experience using experience-led design thinking to improve service delivery and the people experience.
CHRP, CHRL or equivalent HR designation, completed or in progress..

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in financial services or another regulated environment.
Experience leading an HR technology portfolio and/or a shared-services or service-delivery transformation.
Experience with ServiceNow HRSD or a comparable enterprise service-management platform.
Experience in digital product management and AI or automation implementation.
Lean, Six Sigma or service-management certification such as ITIL.

As this position is posted in Montréal, Toronto and Winnipeg, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English. 

Benefits

COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION & RECOGNITION: competitive base salary, performance-weighted bonus, education/career support, option to join Employee Share Purchase Plan with employer matching component.
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS & INSURANCE: competitive health and dental coverage, flexible plan for you and your family and short-term & long-term disability plans.
RETIREMENT SAVINGS PROGRAMS: voluntary Defined Contribution Pension Plan
WORK LIFE BALANCE: paid volunteer days, competitive time off, including 10 wellness days off, WorkPerks discount program, hybrid & flex work arrangements.
INCLUSIVE CULTURE AND DIVERSITY: living our core values: Be a Team, Be Accountable, Be Better, engaging with community through Business Resource Groups (BRG communities are volunteer employee-led groups formed around a common interest, identity, or background).

IGM is a diverse workplace committed to doing business inclusively - this starts with having a representative workforce! We encourage applications from all qualified candidates that represent the diversity present across Canada – including racialized persons, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ community, gender diverse and neurodiverse individuals, as well as all who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas.

Mackenzie Investments is an accessible employer committed to providing barrier -free recruitment experience. If you require accommodation or this information in an alternate format at any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team who will work with you to meet your needs .

How to Apply: Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and a cover letter detailing their qualifications and experience to https://www.ig.ca/en/careers

We thank all applicants for their interest in IG Wealth Management; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Artificial Intelligence in Recruitment: As part of our Talent Acquisition process, we may use artificial intelligence and automated tools to support activities such as candidate sourcing, application review, and interview scheduling. These tools support the recruitment process; all hiring decisions are made by people.

Please apply before November 13 2026.

jobs.title: Director - Finance, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
About The Foundation

At the St. Joseph’s Health Centre Foundation we are committed to continuing to transform St. Joe’s as a leading community hospital that delivers the best care experiences to Toronto’s west end. We are guided by our mission to inspire philanthropy from our community and raise the funds needed to support that transformation.

St. Joe’s has provided care for millions of people in Toronto’s west end for more than a century. Today it is one Canada’s busiest community teaching hospitals, looking after a vibrant community of over half a million.

The Foundation has grown in recent years to be a leading community hospital foundation with a strong and engaged board of directors. We are looking for a new team member to help with gift management and donor engagement that helps to deliver the best care possible for our community.

About The Position

The Director, Finance, Data & Analytics provides strategic and operational leadership across financial management, business intelligence, fundraising analytics and organizational performance for the Foundation.

As the Foundation enters an ambitious next phase of campaign growth, this role will be responsible for ensuring that the organization has the financial discipline, data infrastructure and insights required to support informed decision-making and maximize fundraising performance.

Working closely with the President & CEO, VP, Operations, Senior Leadership Team and fundraising leaders, the Director will connect financial and fundraising data to provide a clear, timely and actionable view of organizational and campaign performance.

The Director will be the Foundation’s lead resource for financial reporting, fundraising analytics, campaign intelligence, data quality and performance reporting, ensuring that leaders have the information they need to identify opportunities, manage risk, allocate resources and achieve campaign objectives.

The successful candidate will combine strong financial expertise with an analytical and business-oriented mindset, an understanding of fundraising and donor data, and the ability to translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Management
Lead the Foundation’s financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and reporting processes.
Prepare timely, accurate decision-useful financial reports for the President & CEO, Senior Leadership Team, Finance Committee and Board.
Monitor financial performance against budget and provide analysis of material variances, trends, risks and opportunities.
Lead the annual budgeting and collaborate on the business planning process with the VP, Operations and Senior Leadership Team.
Oversee cash flow, investments, receivables, payables and other core financial management activities.
Lead the annual audit and maintain strong financial controls, policies and procedures.
Ensure appropriate financial oversight of designated funds, restricted gifts, commitments and disbursements.
Work closely with external accounting and investment partners as required.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, regulatory requirements and Foundation policies.
Campaign & Fundraising Analytics
Own the development and ongoing management of the Foundation’s campaign reporting and fundraising analytics framework.
Partner with fundraising leadership to establish clear definitions, methodologies and performance measures for campaign pipeline, proposals, asks, commitments and revenue.
Develop and maintain campaign dashboards that provide management and Board-level visibility into campaign progress and future potential.
Provide analysis that identifies emerging gaps, opportunities and trends and supports proactive campaign management.
Develop forecasting models to support campaign revenue projections and scenario planning.
Work with fundraising leaders to assess portfolio capacity, prospect movement and pipeline sufficiency.
Translate fundraising data into concise insights and recommendations for the Senior Leadership Team, Campaign Leadership, Finance Committee and Board.
Data Strategy, Quality & Business Intelligence
Serve as the Foundation’s internal lead for data strategy, data governance and business intelligence.
Establish standards for data quality, consistency, definitions and reporting across financial and fundraising systems and oversee implantation with Database Manager.
Partner with fundraising and operations teams to improve the use of Raiser's Edge NXT and other systems as strategic management tools.
Identify opportunities to automate reporting and improve data accessibility.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools using appropriate business intelligence platforms.
Connect financial, fundraising, donor and operational data to provide a more complete picture of organizational performance.
Establish appropriate data governance, privacy, security and access practices in partnership with organizational leadership.
Identify technology and systems improvements that will increase efficiency, insight and fundraising productivity.
Prospect & Donor Intelligence
Support the fundraising team with data-driven prospect identification, qualification and prioritization.
Develop reporting to help assess prospect capacity, relationship activity, portfolio composition and movement through the fundraising cycle.
Partner with fundraising leadership to identify gaps in prospect pipelines and opportunities for portfolio development.
Support analysis of donor behaviour, giving patterns, retention, upgrades and other trends that inform fundraising strategy.
Organizational Performance & Decision Support
Working with VP, Operations develop a consistent framework of organizational KPIs aligned with the Foundation’s strategic and business plans.
Provide analysis to support resource allocation, staffing decisions, event and program performance, fundraising investments and operational planning.
Identify trends and insights across revenue, expenses, fundraising activity and organizational performance.
Prepare clear, concise analysis and visualizations for leadership and Board audiences.
Act as a strategic thought partner to leaders, moving beyond reporting results to helping the organization understand what the data means and what action it should inform.
Leadership, Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
Lead continuous improvement of financial and fundraising reporting processes.
Provide leadership and coaching to the administration team, including the Database Manager.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, automate repetitive activities and improve organizational efficiency.
Contribute to a culture of accountability, curiosity, continuous learning and evidence-informed decision-making.
Provide leadership and coaching to staff, contractors or external resources supporting finance, data and analytics.

Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Our Story & Purpose

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.  
As the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,300 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement, apply today!   

Your Role in Supporting Our Members

As the Director, Strategic Insights
, you will lead the Strategic Insights team within the Analytics Centre of Excellence and oversee how the organization engages with analytics to support informed, evidence-based decision-making. You will partner with leaders across the organization to scope analytics work, execute the analytics strategy, and advance Vancity’s data utilization and advanced analytics capabilities.  
You will play a critical role in translating complex insights into meaningful recommendations, strengthening analytical practices, and helping teams use data effectively to achieve organizational priorities.  
This is a full-time, permanent
role based out of Vancity Head Office
and will report directly to the Vice President, Analytics Centre of Excellence
.  While this position provides a hybrid
work arrangement, you will be expected to be on-site for events and business demands.

How You’ll Make an Impact

Providing strategic leadership and direction for the Strategic Insights function and its evolving priorities  

Leading the execution of the Analytics Centre of Excellence strategy in partnership with teams across the organization  

Developing frameworks, practices, and approaches that support organizational objectives across multiple divisions  

Guiding the effective use of analytics by educating stakeholders and briefing subject-matter experts on analytical findings and recommendations  

Influencing business decisions and organizational strategies through relevant analytics methodologies and evidence-based insights  

Advising senior leaders and making recommendations that help shape strategic priorities and decision-making  

Identifying opportunities to improve current practices and strengthen how insights are applied across the organization  

Building trusted relationships with business leaders and supporting the strategic vision of the Analytics Centre of Excellence  

Leading ongoing enterprise communications that promote an analytical mindset and share progress  

Building an engaged, capable, and efficient Strategic Insights team while managing evolving talent and skill requirements   

What You’ll Bring to the Team

Significant experience leading strategic insights, business intelligence, analytics, data strategy, or a related function  

Demonstrated experience translating complex data and analysis into clear recommendations for senior leaders and business stakeholders  

Strong people-leadership experience, including building team capability, setting priorities, and supporting employee development  

Experience developing and implementing analytics frameworks, methodologies, and organizational best practices  

Proven ability to influence enterprise-level decisions and work effectively across multiple business areas  

Strong relationship-management, consultation, and executive communication skills  

Sound judgment and the ability to balance strategic priorities, organizational risk, and member needs  

A degree in business, analytics, economics, data science, finance, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience  

Extra Skills That Set You Apart

Experience working in financial services, a credit union, or another highly regulated environment  

Experience leading an analytics centre of excellence or enterprise-wide analytics function  

Knowledge of advanced analytics, data utilization, predictive modelling, or machine-learning practices  

Experience supporting organizational change and strengthening data literacy across diverse stakeholder groups  

You’ll Thrive Here If You Are

A strategic thinker
who connects analytics, business priorities, and member needs to support better decisions.  

An influential communicator
who makes complex information clear, relevant, and actionable for different audiences.  

A collaborative leader
who builds trusted relationships and brings people together around shared goals.  

A people-focused manager
who develops talent, encourages innovation, and creates a safe and respectful team environment.  

We value lived experience, so if you are interested in this role, we encourage you to apply even if you feel your skills don’t perfectly align with those listed. 

What You’ll Earn

This role offers a salary range of $148,000 to $191,500 per annum
. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.

A career at Vancity is more than just a job. You’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:  
Living Wage Employer:
We’re the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada and consistently ranked among Canada’s Top Employers
